summary: Modern agents can navigate large corpora through tools, and mechanical splitting may make the behavior harder to follow.

points.text: A coding-agent study found that tool-using agents could navigate very large text corpora with file-system search and scripts, outperforming published long-context baselines on its text tasks. It did not measure code changes in a single large class.
Moving methods into thin wrappers or partial files can increase cross-file jumps while leaving state, lifecycle and invariant coupling intact.
LongCodeBench compares different real issues across context-length brackets in a single-shot setup; its declining patch success is not a causal estimate of the effect of one file growing.
No controlled before-and-after study here demonstrates that decomposing one large service improves the success rate of current frontier coding agents.
